info.name: Shree Astro — Admin Panel
info.description:
Everything **admin_panel** calls.

## Start here
1. Seed the admin: `npm run seed:admin` in the backend folder. That gives you `admin@shreeastro.com` / `admin@123`.
2. Select the **Shree Astro — Local** environment.
3. Run *2 · Sign in → Admin login*. The token is saved, and the console prints which permissions the account holds.

## Permissions
Every route needs a permission, not just an admin token — a Finance admin can read payments but cannot approve astrologers, and gets a **403** if they try. Each request below says which permission it needs. The role-to-permission map is in `models/Admin.js`; `super_admin` has all of them.

## The approval flow
*5 · Astrologers* is the panel's main job, and the order matters: approve the documents and the bank account, then approve the application — that last step is what mints the astro code, sets the opening rates, and puts the astrologer into the seeker's directory.

## Auditing
Every change here writes an audit row automatically. Check *10 · Audit logs* after running anything in this collection.

request.description: Is the server up and is Mongo connected? Note this one sits outside /api/v1.

Email and password — the only account type that uses one. Seed it with `npm run seed:admin`, which creates `admin@shreeastro.com` / `admin@123`.

The tokens are also set as httpOnly cookies, which is what the browser panel actually uses; the body is here so Postman can work too.

A wrong email and a wrong password give the **same** answer, so the form cannot be used to discover which addresses are admins. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes.

item.name: 5 · Astrologers

request.description:
**The short form.** Four fields and nothing else:

- `email` — the address they sign in with. This is the whole identity.
- `commissionPercent` — the platform's cut. Omit it and the platform default from Settings is used.
- `availability` — free text, e.g. "Mon–Sat · 9 AM – 9 PM".
- `status` — `approved` (listed) or `blocked` (hidden).

Everything else — name, phone, photo, languages, expertise, experience, about and **rates** — the astrologer fills in themselves from the profile screen in their own app.

The account is approved on creation, so there is no application to review. A placeholder name is derived from the email until they set their real one, and an astro code is minted immediately.

They will **not appear in the seeker's directory** until they have set at least one rate — listing someone who cannot be consulted is worse than not listing them.

Refusals: 400 on a malformed email or a commission outside 0–100, 409 if that email already has an account.

request.description: Send `rejected` with a `reason` to turn it down instead. Needs `astrologers.approve`.
A payout cannot be requested against an unapproved account.

The decision that puts an astrologer into the seeker's directory.

It also **mints their astro code** and **sets their opening rates** — without at least one service they cannot take work, so send the services here.

`ratePerMinute` is the list price and `offerPercent` is the discount struck through it. Needs `astrologers.approve`.

request.description: The reason is shown back in the astrologer's app, and they can no longer sign in.
Takes them offline and out of the directory at once. Needs `astrologers.manage`.

Approving is what actually writes the new rate onto the service — an astrologer can never set it themselves.

If the request had `applyToAll`, every service is repriced. Needs `astrologers.manage`.

request.description: Every session with who was in it, how long it ran, what it cost and how it was rated. Needs `consultations.view`.

For a session that is stuck or being abused. It runs through the ordinary end-a-chat path, so the seeker is still charged for the time that actually elapsed and the astrologer is still paid — this is not the same as cancelling. Needs `consultations.manage`.

request.description:
Puts the money back as a **new credit row** — the original charge is never edited. The ledger is a history, and history does not change.

Only a successful debit can be refunded, and only once (409 on a second try). Needs `payments.refund`.
Seekers and astrologers in one table, biggest balance first. Needs `wallets.view`.

request.description:
A hand-made credit or debit. It goes through the same `post()` every other movement uses, so it lands in the ledger like anything else and the running balance stays correct.

The reason is **required** — the row records who made the adjustment and why, and there is no way to make an untraceable one. Needs `wallets.adjust`.
Needs `wallets.view`.

item.name: 11 · Settings

request.description: Commission, recharge limits, minimum payout, free trial minutes, payout cycle, feature switches and app versions. Needs `settings.view`.

Send only what changed. `features` and `appVersions` merge one key at a time, so sending a single switch does not clear the rest.

These are live: the recharge limits govern the very next top-up. Needs `settings.manage`.

request.description: `signOutEverywhere: true` also invalidates every token that account is currently holding. You cannot suspend your own account.
Suspends rather than deletes — audit rows point at this record, and a log that names a missing admin is worth less. You cannot revoke your own access.

Everything the Reports page draws: new users and astrologers, the day-by-day activity trend, how people signed up, the most-asked topics, the top-earning astrologers and the business summary.

All of it is counted from the data rather than stored, so the numbers cannot drift out of step with what happened. Needs `reports.view`.
